title: What can you say about vitamin B6 in your ads and on your site?
summary: The library supports 8 wordings for vitamin B6; the strongest is "Supports normal energy-yielding metabolism" (strong, 0.21-100 mg a day). Avoid wording that names or implies a disease, a drug or a treatment, such as "Treats PCOS, or balances hormones in PCOS".

supported_wordings.why: Listed by Health Canada and authorized in the EU after EFSA review.
supported_wordings.dose_details: Adults 19 and older. Health Canada: 0.1-100 mg a day (80 mg at 18). EU: at least 0.21 mg, 15% of the 1.4 mg EU reference value (Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011, Annex XIII). ODS upper limit: 100 mg.
supported_wordings.form: Pyridoxine hydrochloride or pyridoxal 5'-phosphate, counted as vitamin B6

wordings_to_avoid.wording: Treats PCOS, or balances hormones in PCOS

wordings_to_avoid.why: Names medical conditions: premenstrual dysphoric disorder and depression.

wordings_to_avoid.wording: Lowers homocysteine to protect the heart, or reduces the risk of heart disease
wordings_to_avoid.why: Names a disease. FDA's qualified claim on B vitamins and vascular disease has set wording (see fda_health_claims).

wordings_to_avoid.wording: Treats carpal tunnel syndrome or nerve damage (neuropathy)

evidence_strengths.strong: At least two listed sources support it independently at a comparable dose and form, and none disagrees.
evidence_strengths.moderate: One listed source supports it as an evidence-based use at that dose, and no listed source disagrees.
evidence_strengths.limited: The only support is traditional use, the sources disagree, or the source itself calls the evidence weak.

reasons_to_avoid.drug: names a drug or presents the product as one
reasons_to_avoid.treatment: promises to treat, cure or prevent a condition
